newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Israel says it will not be put on trial.
newsitem.headline: Israel says it will not be put on trial.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Friday his country would not accept the blame for the latest Israeli-Palestinian crisis and called on Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to impose order.
"Israel will not allow itself to be placed on trial," Levy told a meeting of the U.N. Security Council in New York.
Arab and European nations have criticized Israel's new right-wing government for stoking tensions that have led to clashes in the West Bank and Gaza in which more than 60 people have died.

Levy denied Israel had reneged on peace agreements but said the government would not change its policy. He called on Arafat to impose his authority give "clear and unequivocal instructions" to his forces to stop the fighting.
The U.N. Security Council, he said, should not stoke tensions further by criticising Israel.
Levy said there had been an "orchestrated attempt to put blame on Israel and to portray her as the sole responsible party for the bitter harvest of bloodshed".
